title: Check out three directories from a monorepo, not all forty
summary: Your team owns two services in a huge repository. Sparse-checkout gives you only those directories on disk, while git still has the full history.
mental_model: Sparse-checkout changes what lands in your working tree, not what is in the repository. Every commit, branch and file is still there — git simply skips writing most of them to disk.

steps.title: See everything you did not ask for
steps.why: Five services, a library and docs. In a real monorepo this is tens of thousands of files, most of which your editor will index and your search will trawl through.
steps.expect: Every path in the repository, on disk.

steps.title: Turn on cone-mode sparse checkout
steps.why: Cone mode restricts patterns to whole directories, which keeps it fast on huge trees. Immediately after init, only root-level files remain in the working tree.
steps.expect: Root files only on disk — but ls-files still lists everything, because the repository is unchanged.

verify.label: the service directories left the working tree

steps.title: Ask for the directories you own
steps.why: `set` replaces the list with the paths you name. Their parents come along automatically, and everything else stays out of the working tree.
steps.expect: payments and libs/common present; catalog, search and billing absent.

verify.label: the ones you do not own are not on disk

steps.title: Prove the rest is still in git
steps.why: `git show` reads a file you cannot see on disk, and `git log` covers commits touching it. Nothing was removed from history — this is a working-tree feature only.
steps.expect: Content and history for files that are not on your disk.

steps.title: Add a directory without retyping the list
steps.why: `add` appends to the cone. Use it when a task drags you into a neighbouring service for an afternoon.

steps.title: Commits still cover everything
steps.why: Changing a file you can see commits normally, and files outside the cone are untouched rather than deleted. A sparse checkout cannot accidentally delete the rest of the monorepo.

verify.label: the commit touched only what you edited
…and every other path is still tracked

steps.title: Turn it off again
steps.why: `disable` restores the full working tree. Nothing was lost, and the repository never knew the difference — which is what makes sparse-checkout safe to experiment with.

verify.label: you committed normally while sparsely checked out
verify.hint: sparse-checkout does not restrict what you can commit

verify.label: the commit contains only your service's change
every path is still tracked in the repository
the working tree was restored with sparse-checkout disable

pitfalls: Files outside the cone are marked skip-worktree, not deleted. Tools that scan the working tree will simply not see them — including your own scripts.
Non-cone mode accepts full gitignore-style patterns and is dramatically slower on large repositories. Stay in cone mode unless you truly need patterns.
A merge that touches paths outside your cone still succeeds; you just cannot see the conflict files. Widen the cone before a large merge.
Combine with `git clone --filter=blob:none` for the real monorepo win: fast clone AND small working tree.
